Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for our claim file. Can you please state
your full name for the record?
A: I'd rather just go by my first name for now, if that's all right.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me whree you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in the parking lot of a grocery store in Baytown, Texas. I had just pulled into a spot near the front entrance.
Q: What were you doing at the time of the impact?
A: I was backing out of the space, moving slowly, maybe five or ten miles an hour. The other car was coming down
the aisle, and I didn't see it until it was right there.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle beofre the contact?
A: Not really. There was a shopping cart return blocking part of my view on the right side.
Q: Did you hear or see any horn or warning before the impact?
A: I heard a short beep, but by then it was too late to stop.
Q: Were there any passengers in your vehicle?
A: No, I was alone.
Q: How fast would you say the other car was going?
A: It didn't seem fast. It was probably moving at about the speed of a person walking quickly.
Q: Did you notice any injuries when the collision happened?
A: My back felt a jolt right away. Over the next day it got stiffer and started aching in the lower area, so I went to see a
doctor.
Q: Have you received any treatment since then?
A: I've been doing physical therapy twice a week and taking over-the-counter pain medication. The doctor said it
looks like a back strain.
Q: Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm cooperating fully and I want to get my car repaierd and my back looked after.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
